summary: One read-only Codex cold read (gpt-5.6-terra, task-mu6iscvx-t13i1u; the first launch task-mu6horph-czlyc5 failed at Codex authentication and returned nothing, recorded as the --reread reason) of the measure-filter-foundation task plan and contract against the built repo returned NOT CONVERGED with seven findings. Six were settled from the repository: reopen order is status first over the raw operand union then canonicalisation of a runnable selection only; ErrorPayload.details is widened in the contract to carry a typed reason and the saved and pin ExplorationErrorDto documents it; the equivalence proof across provider, direct Ask and stored re-run moves to task 2 while task 1 proves stored, save and pin handling; the backend/src/chat exception is made explicit (selectionExecutor.ts, its composed test, chat.schemas.ts and its test) and the review budget raised to 26 files / 1500 lines; totalsOverAliases is specified as two concrete per-domain CASE expressions over SUM(actual)/SUM(budget) and SUM(actual_net)/SUM(budget_net) with leaves for both; normalisation is lexical (split, pad, keep integer digits, canonical negative zero) with a MAX_SAFE_INTEGER leaf. One finding went to the human: the shared selection schema is also the Ask request schema, so a direct /api/chat request could reach the new SQL path before task 2; the human chose to keep Ask closed in task 1 with its own strict schema that refuses measureFilters, lifted by task 2. The task plan and contract were amended once and this pass is recorded against the amended version.
gaps: Shared-schema sequencing was unsafe: task 1 widens selectionSchema, which chat.schemas.ts imports for the Ask request, while Ask canonicalisation is deferred to task 2, so a direct /api/chat request could reach the new SQL path without normalisation or visible operand appending.

Reopen behaviour contradicted stale-selection behaviour: canonicalising a stored selection whose operand was removed from the registry would throw unknown_measure where the contract requires definition_unregistered.
The promised HTTP envelope did not type-check: ErrorPayload.details permits only fieldErrors, not { reason }, and the saved/pin error Swagger was left undocumented.
The saved-service leaf could not prove equivalence with a direct selection: the direct path belongs to ChatService in task 2.

Scope was self-contradictory and the review cap unattainable: the contract forbade backend/src/chat changes yet required selectionExecutor.ts, and the edits total at least 23 files against a 16-file budget.
totalsOverAliases was under-specified across domains: governed aliases are actual/budget while statement aliases are actual_net/budget_net, so one literal CASE cannot serve both.

Fixed-scale normalisation was not stated to be lexical: Number(...).toFixed(2) would round valid thresholds above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER into a different comparison and would not canonicalise negative zero.
contradictions: Contract 'no file under backend/src/chat changes' versus the required edit to selectionExecutor.ts and its composed test.
Contract 'canonicalise on reopen before status' versus 'an unregistered operand reports definition_unregistered'.
resolutions: Ask stays closed until task 2 (human ruling): chat.schemas.ts gets its own strict selection schema omitting measureFilters, a chat.schemas.test.ts leaf proves the 400, task 2 lifts it; chat.schemas.ts and its test join the write scope and the chat exception list.

Reopen order fixed in the contract and plan: status first over the raw operand union, then canonicalisation of a runnable selection only; a leaf proves a removed operand reports definition_unregistered.

Contract widens ErrorPayload.details to { fieldErrors?; reason?: MeasureFilterInvalidReason } with the enum exported from the contract; the saved and pin ExplorationErrorDto documents the reason member; the envelope leaf pins it.
Proof split: the task 1 saved leaf proves store refusal, canonicalisation and the reopen status; the provider/direct/stored equivalence leaf is task 2's.

Scope made explicit: under backend/src/chat exactly selectionExecutor.ts, selectionExecutor.composed.test.ts, chat.schemas.ts and chat.schemas.test.ts; review budget 26 files / 1500 lines with the reason enumerating the surface.

totalsOverAliases specified per domain: governed-financial.percentage over SUM(actual)/SUM(budget), mis-statement.percentage over SUM(actual_net)/SUM(budget_net), the same nil-rule CASE; a leaf covers both domains.

Normalisation is lexical and BigInt-safe: split on the point, pad the fraction, keep integer digits verbatim, canonicalise negative zero to 0.00, never Number() or toFixed; the helper leaf asserts a value above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER and negative zero.
Contradiction (chat scope) resolved by naming the four permitted chat files in the contract and reviewer focus.
Contradiction (reopen order) resolved by the status-first rule above.

rounds.question: The task cold read found that the shared selection schema is also the Ask request schema, so once task 1 widens it a direct /api/chat request could carry a measure filter into the new SQL path before task 2 adds Ask's canonicalisation and refusal. How should task 1 handle that gap?
options: Bring minimal Ask handling into task 1

current_flow: Today: Selection (contract/src/measure.ts:151) carries measureIds, dimensionIds, filters (dimension eq/in/neq), timeWindow and limit; the Bedrock selector emits it through emit_selection with no comparison shape; chat.service.ts validates it through validateSelectionForUser (selectionValidation.ts:5, measureIds only), the executor authorizes on measureIds and runs sqlBuilder.build (WHERE dimension filters, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, LIMIT; no HAVING) then totalsFor re-runs the ungrouped query itself; buildStatementProjection never reads selection.filters; saved.service.ts and pins.service.ts store the zod-parsed selection and compute runnable status and the pin definition-version hash from measureIds; the global exception filter maps a BadRequestException to HTTP_400 with a fixed message and empty details. A question asking for Actual above Budget therefore has no shape and comes back unfiltered with the verified badge.

new_abstractions: A measure comparison filter on the selection contract, compiled to HAVING over verified expressions — the first row condition on aggregates the model can select without authoring SQL.
One pure canonicaliser helper and one typed exception that every selection ingress calls — the first single seam for selection normalisation and operand authorization.
A builder-owned totals query over a derived table with per-measure totalsOverAliases — the first totals that respect a row filter beyond the visible page.
